trust_decision.summary: The decoder decides whether an attacker-supplied PFX is authentic by recomputing the PKCS#12 MAC with a key derived from the file's own PBKDF2 parameters; the fix makes that decision reject a PBMAC1 key length below 20 bytes instead of accepting any positive length.

landing_point.why: The summary says "Authentication bypass in Decode functions", so an engineer starts at the exported Decode/DecodeChain API; the MAC decision is two calls away in getSafeContents (pkcs12.go:550) and the actual key-length sink is in another file, mac.go:130.

fix_sites.entry_point: pkcs12.Decode, pkcs12.DecodeChain, pkcs12.DecodeTrustStore, pkcs12.ToPEM (all reach getSafeContents -> verifyMac -> doMac -> doPBMAC1)
fix_sites.module_kind: library public API into an unexported MAC helper in the root package

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No O2 site and no O8 route exists: every decode entry point funnels through the single verifyMac call at pkcs12.go:573 into doPBMAC1, and the encoder side always writes KeyLength 32 (mac.go:50), so there is no route a solver could argue is out of scope.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A PFX with no MacData at all is accepted when the caller passes an empty password (passwordless files produced by the Passwordless encoder); a fix that makes a verified MAC mandatory on decode breaks this documented behaviour.

O6_input_shapes: explicit PBMAC1 PBKDF2 keyLength of 1-19 inside the MAC AlgorithmIdentifier parameters (the shape the fix rejects)
absent or non-positive keyLength, already rejected before the fix by the neighbouring check
keyLength of 20 or more, including the encoder's own value of 32, which must keep verifying

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A PBES2 consumer that honours kdfParams.KeyLength instead of the encryption-scheme-fixed 16/24/32 (crypto.go:240-250) and derives an attacker-chosen-length AES key.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The same pbkdf2Params type (crypto.go:200-205) is parsed for both PBMAC1 (mac.go:85-88) and PBES2 (crypto.go:217-220); RFC 8018 lets PBES2 carry keyLength, the field is parsed and silently ignored today, so a maintainer adding interop for files that set it would naturally use it and would need the same floor.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An encoder-side PBMAC1 parameter builder (a new encoder variant or an option) that emits a key length below the MAC digest size instead of the hard-coded 32.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This tree just gained a new encoder variant with its own PBMAC1 parameters (Modern2026, pkcs12.go:185-193), so another variant carrying its own makePBMAC1Parameters-style builder is a normal change.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A companion PBMAC1 policy check on the PRF (reject the implicit SHA-1 default in the same validation block as the key-length floor).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The PRF switch already enumerates HMAC-SHA1 and an ASN.1 default of SHA-1 (mac.go:101-105); a maintainer tightening PBMAC1 parameter policy writes such checks in exactly this block.

O9_family: Improper input validation of untrusted KDF parameters leading to authentication bypass (CWE-20 / CWE-287)

O10_build.toolchain: go 1.19 module (go.mod:3) with golang.org/x/crypto v0.11.0 (go.mod:5, go.sum:6-7); `go build ./...` / `go test ./...`
O10_build.project_tests: pkcs12_pbmac1_test.go exercises the RFC 9579 A.1-A.6 vectors through getSafeContents, including the missing-KeyLength error text (pkcs12_pbmac1_test.go:151-169); mac_test.go:76-148 tests PBMAC1 compute/verify; pkcs12_test.go round-trips Encode/Decode and trust stores.

j.j_sites_touched: mac.go (doPBMAC1 is the single internal choke point that all four exported decode paths reach)
j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add the floor as `KeyLength == 32` (the encoder's own value) rather than `>= 20`, or check it in Decode/getSafeContents instead of the shared doPBMAC1, so interoperable files with other legal key lengths stop decoding.

out_of_scope_notes: getSafeContents accepts a PFX with no MacData at all when the password is empty (pkcs12.go:569-572); this is deliberate and documented (pkcs12.go:507-508, Passwordless at pkcs12.go:127-138), and it is not the PBMAC1 key-strength property this advisory fixes, so it was not pursued as a route.
unverified: Repository size in MB could not be measured without a shell; the tree is 17 short Go files plus six small base64 testdata files, so tiny_repo is asserted on that basis rather than on a measured byte count.
The RFC 9579 testdata vectors were not DER-decoded, so it is unconfirmed whether any of them uses a KeyLength below 20 that a stricter-than-published fix would break.
j_multi_site is set to 1 by the stated O1>=2 rule; in reality all four exported entry points share the one check site in mac.go, so no second source site needs the fix.
